results.corrected_extracted: The Discussion gives a population attributable risk of 7.2%, or 413,326 young-adult cases of depression in the USA potentially attributable to cannabis (70,872,118 people aged 18 to 34 x 8.1% x 7.2%), without a stated method; the figure assumes causation and uses a 2-week prevalence of depression among US adults over 20 (8.1%) as an incidence. Editors' reconstruction: Levin's formula with the pooled OR 1.37 taken as a relative risk and the 20.9% past-month use among US adolescents cited in the same paragraph gives 7.18%, i.e. the highest-use odds ratio treated as the effect of any past-month use (study card reporting issue).
results.note: Numbers, the correction notice ('young adult' cases) and the 2-week prevalence confirmed; 413,326 recomputed. 'Treats the highest-use OR as any past-month use' is not stated by the source: it is the editors' reconstruction (7.18%), now labelled. No number changed.
